pages.text: Something Is Here
pages.subtext: The Star Door Mystery
pages.alt: Mia, Sol and Tavi stand near the shut Star Door and its five-star map. Nori, the friend they will meet during the adventure, is nearby.

pages.alt: Mia, Tavi and Sol stand in the library beside the empty map stand.

pages.text:
High above the sleeping town stood a tower full of starry rooms.

Before breakfast, three friends met inside: Mia, Sol and Tavi.
pages.subtext: Mia loved questions. Sol loved surprises. Tavi loved looking closely.
pages.alt: Mia, Sol and Tavi meet in a warm, starry tower room before breakfast.

pages.text:
At the heart of the tower stood the Star Door. It opened when a new adventure was ready.

This morning, it was shut. Then a note came through its letter box and landed with a soft tap.
pages.subtext: The note landed beside Mia. Point to the note and the letter box.
pages.alt: A paper note lies beside Mia after coming through the shut Star Door's letter box. The note and letter box are clearly labelled.

pages.text:
Mia picked it up. “A message for us!” she said. Then she read it aloud:

FIND NOTHING.
FIVE CLUES WILL SHOW THE WAY.
pages.subtext: Sol blinked. “How do we find nothing?” Tavi smiled. “Let’s look carefully and see.” An optional book code is hiding in the picture.
pages.alt: Mia holds the open note so Sol and Tavi can see it. The message says FIND NOTHING. FIVE CLUES WILL SHOW THE WAY. The optional code ROOMSTAR is hidden in the scene.

pages.text:
The wall shimmered. A map appeared with five pale stars.

“One clue for each star,” said Mia. “When we learn what a clue shows us, its star will shine.”
pages.subtext: A glowing arrow pointed to a small parcel. Follow the arrow with your finger.
pages.alt: A magical map above Mia, Sol and Tavi shows five pale star shapes and one bright arrow pointing to a small, closed parcel.

pages.text:
The friends followed the arrow. Sol lifted the lid.

“My teddy!” he cheered.

Point to the teddy. Now pretend to lift it out and place it beside the box.
pages.subtext: First notice what is inside. Then make the move.
pages.alt: Sol's brown teddy is clearly visible inside the open box while Mia and Tavi watch.

pages.text:
The teddy sat beside the box. The box had not moved.

Sol peered inside. “What is inside the box now?”
pages.subtext: Look inside. Point to the box and the teddy. Then answer.
pages.alt: Sol's teddy sits beside the open box. The empty inside of the box is easy to see.

pages.text:
THE TEDDY IS OUTSIDE.
THE BOX IS STILL HERE.

“The box is empty,” said Tavi. “Empty means there is no teddy inside. The box is still here.”
pages.subtext: You checked what moved and what stayed. Star one shone gold. Can you spot the optional book code?
pages.alt: The open, empty box and the teddy beside it are clearly labelled. The box is still present, and the first map star glows gold.

pages.text:
The map’s next arrow led through a blue door to a room full of bells.

A small purple guide waved. “I’m Nori. I listen carefully. I can help with this clue.”
pages.subtext: Mia, Sol and Tavi said hello. Nori joined them for the rest of this adventure.
pages.alt: Mia, Sol and Tavi enter the bell room and meet Nori, the one new friend joining this adventure.

pages.text:
The biggest bell swung once and rang. Then it stopped.

“Cup your hand to your ear,” said Nori. “Listen carefully. What is the bell doing now?”
pages.subtext: What can you hear? Is the bell ringing now? Listen before you answer.
pages.alt: Nori, Mia, Sol and Tavi listen beside the large bell after it has stopped moving and ringing.

pages.text:
“The bell did not ring while we listened,” said Nori. “It was quiet, but it was still here.”

Sol whispered, “I can still hear my breathing.”
pages.subtext: You listened before answering. A quiet bell is not nothing. Star two shone gold. Can you spot the optional code?
pages.alt: Nori and the three friends listen beside the quiet bell, which is still clearly present. The second map star glows gold.

pages.text:
The next arrow led to the paper room.

On a table lay a white card and a pencil. Mia picked up the card. “There are no marks on it yet.”
pages.subtext: First look at the card. What is there? What is not on it?
pages.alt: Mia holds a white card with no marks. A pencil lies on the table while Sol, Tavi and Nori look closely.

pages.text:
Choose one. Pretend to draw a mark on the card, or leave the card just as it is.

In either choice, is the card still there?
pages.subtext: Point to the card before you turn the page.
pages.alt: The white card and pencil are ready for the child to imagine either drawing one mark or leaving the card unchanged.

pages.text:
IF WE DRAW: the card has a mark.
IF WE DO NOT DRAW: the card has no mark.

A card with no marks is blank. It is still a card.
pages.subtext: You compared two choices and checked what stayed. Star three shone gold. Can you spot the optional code?
pages.alt: One white card has a mark and one white card is blank. Both cards remain visible and clearly labelled while the third map star glows.

pages.text:
Seven blank tiles lit up on the wall.

“One tile for each letter,” said Sol. “Maybe the next clue can show us the word on the note.”
pages.subtext: The tiles blinked from left to right, ready for the next clue.
pages.alt: Mia, Sol, Tavi and Nori look up as seven blank wall tiles light from left to right.

pages.text:
Start at the left. Point to each tile:

N   O   T   H   I   N   G

Now say the whole word: nothing.
pages.subtext: You are building one word from seven letters. Point, say, then turn.
pages.alt: Seven large tiles spell N O T H I N G from left to right above Mia, Sol, Tavi and Nori.

pages.text:
“The letters make the word nothing,” said Tavi.

Mia tapped the tiles. “We can see the word on the tiles. But a written word is not an object called nothing.”
pages.subtext: You found the written word, not a new object. Star four shone gold.
pages.alt: The seven visible letter tiles still spell NOTHING while Mia points to them. The fourth map star glows gold.

pages.text:
The fourth star sent a beam of light along a hallway. The friends followed it to a red curtain.

Sol’s teddy slipped from his bag and rolled behind the open curtain.
pages.subtext: Everyone watched the teddy stop behind the curtain.
pages.alt: Mia, Sol, Tavi and Nori watch Sol's teddy roll across the floor and stop behind the open red curtain.

pages.text:
Nori pulled the curtain closed. The teddy was out of sight.

“We cannot see it now,” said Mia. “Did it stop being there?”
pages.subtext: Think about what you just saw. Decide before you turn.
pages.alt: The closed red curtain hides the teddy. Mia, Sol, Tavi and Nori remain visible in front of it.

pages.text:
Mia slowly opened the curtain. First one paw appeared. Then two ears. Then—there was the teddy!

“It was hidden,” said Mia. “It stayed there, even when we could not see it.”
pages.subtext: Hidden does not mean gone. You checked by opening the curtain. Star five shone gold. Find the optional code.
pages.alt: The red curtain opens slowly to reveal Sol's teddy, which stayed behind it. The teddy and open curtain are labelled, and the fifth map star glows gold.

pages.text:
All five stars flashed—one, two, three, four, five. The Star Door opened into a room with two little doors.

“One last check,” said Tavi.
pages.subtext: The friends went through together.
pages.alt: All five map stars glow as the Star Door opens. Beyond it, Mia, Sol, Tavi and Nori can see two smaller doors.

pages.text:
Behind Door A was a shelf with a white card.
Behind Door B was a shelf with no card.

Point to the card. Then point to both shelves.
pages.subtext: Which things can you see? Look before you answer.
pages.alt: Door A contains a shelf and a white card. Door B contains a shelf with no card. Both doors and both shelves are easy to see.

pages.text:
Mia asked, “What did we find?”
Door A: a door, a shelf and a card.
Door B: a door and an empty shelf.
Did we find an object called nothing?
pages.subtext: Say what is there. Then say what is missing from Door B.
pages.alt: Door A's card and shelf are labelled. Door B's empty shelf is labelled. Both doors remain visible.

pages.text:
“Door A has a card,” said Sol. “Door B has an empty shelf.”

“Both doors and both shelves are still here,” said Tavi. “We did not find an object called nothing.”
pages.subtext: You named what was there and what was missing. The mystery is solved! Find the final optional code.
pages.alt: Mia, Sol, Tavi and Nori stand between the two open doors. One shelf holds a card and one shelf is empty. The optional code TWODOORS is hidden near the map.

pages.text:
Mia read the note again: FIND NOTHING.

They had found an empty box, a quiet bell, a blank card, a written word and a hidden teddy. They never found an object called nothing.
pages.subtext: The clues taught us to say exactly what was there, what changed and what we could not see or hear.
pages.alt: Mia holds the original note beside the completed five-star map while Sol, Tavi and Nori remember all five clues.

pages.text:
The friends took the five-star map to the library. Tavi placed the box and teddy on a table.

“Which one became empty when we moved the teddy?”
pages.subtext: Point to the box or the teddy. Use the first clue to help you.
pages.alt: Tavi asks a remembering question beside two clear choices: an open box and Sol's teddy outside it. Mia, Sol and Nori are nearby.

pages.text:
“The box,” said Tavi. “It became empty because the teddy moved out.”

The teddy changed place. The box stayed in the room.
pages.subtext: Remembering a clue helps you use the lesson again.
pages.alt: The open, empty box and the teddy outside it are clearly labelled in the library. Mia, Sol, Tavi and Nori recall what changed.

pages.text:
Mia put the finished map in its library stand. Nori rang one soft bell to celebrate.

“We looked, listened, tried and checked,” said Mia. “That is how we solved the mystery.”
pages.subtext: Nori promised to visit again when a mystery needed careful listening.
pages.alt: Mia puts the completed five-star map in its library stand while Nori rings one small bell and Sol and Tavi celebrate.

pages.text:
Here is what the mystery taught you:

Empty, quiet, blank and hidden are different. Each word tells us something clear about what we found.

We did not find an object called nothing.
pages.subtext: Why it matters: careful words help other people understand what you saw or heard.
pages.alt: Tavi shows four picture cards for an empty box, a quiet bell, a blank card and a hidden teddy. The completed map is beside them.

pages.text: Just then, a small bell rang. A hatch opened high in the wall. A blue-and-gold parcel slid down the library slide and stopped beside Sol.
pages.subtext: The slide was the tower’s special way of delivering a new adventure.
pages.alt: A blue-and-gold parcel slides from a small hatch, down the library's parcel slide, and stops beside Sol while Mia, Tavi and Nori watch.

pages.text:
Mia read the parcel label aloud:

HOW CAN ONE WHOLE HAVE MANY PARTS?

Sol hugged his teddy. “Let’s find out!”
pages.subtext: Next: Book E02 · One Whole, Many Parts
pages.alt: Mia reads the next adventure's question from the parcel label while Sol hugs his teddy and Tavi and Nori listen in the warm library.
